name: Pale Pink
lede: Pale pink is a very light pink, a rosy tint with much white in it; in painting it can be what is left when a red lake has faded.

sections.title: A tint, not a material
sections.body: Like many pale shades, pale pink is a description. The dictionary defines blancmange pink as a pale pink [1], and St Clair's glossary defines shell as pale pink and magnolia as a pale pink-beige [2]. On screen the swatch is a light, low-chroma tint close to [[misty-rose]], [[light-pink]] and [[baby-pink]] [6].

sections.title: What fading leaves behind
sections.body:
Ball asks how we can know that a patch of pale pink in an old painting once left the brush as rosy carmine lake [3]. In several paintings of one era the red lake has faded entirely, so that robes now look pale pink in the highlights and midtones, which hold a lot of white lead [3]. In the shadows and folds, darkened with ultramarine, the same robes read as deep bluish purple [3]. The pale pink is what remains of a deeper red, and the pigment is not always at fault: the red lake faded [3].

The same process shows how dyes behave. Cochineal dye can be shifted anywhere from pale pink to a nearly black red by the additives used, such as acids or metals like tin [4]. Tens of thousands of dried insects went into a pound of the raw dye [4]. Compare [[carmine]] and [[blush]] [6].

sections.title: Pale pink in other places
sections.body: In Charlotte Brontë's *Villette*, Lucy Snowe insists that a dress described as scarlet was really pink, and pale pink at that, and subdued with black lace [5]. The other character's alarm shows how a faint hint of red could carry weight [5]. A cardinals' consistory miniature in the Pierpont Morgan Library, according to Gage, shows cardinals in grey, pale blue and pale pink, all hatted in vermilion [7]. Finlay met a cotton breeder who found red and pale pink bolls in the genes of naturally brown cotton [8].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
The swatch measures a lightness of 90 and a chroma of about 12, with a hue angle of 13 degrees [6]. Its contrast ratio against white is only 1.3 to 1, so it barely separates from a white page [6]. The nearest named colors are Misty Rose at about 5 units and Mimi Pink at about 6 [6].

We have not computed an archive count. Faded lakes mean that painted pale pinks should be read with care, and screen colors are approximate [6].
